about: Ask this paper eval: questions with answers from the paper's abstract, plus questions the paper can't answer, where the right reply is to say so.

cases.question: How much compute does LOWN save, and how much accuracy does it keep?
cases.reference: It keeps 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score while using 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs on average.

cases.question: Does LOWN need any training?
cases.reference: No. It works without training or a tuned threshold.

cases.question: How often does removing the image change the prediction?
cases.reference: Only at 22.8% of decoding steps on average, and as few as 7.9%.

cases.question: Can it be combined with visual token pruning?
cases.reference: Yes, it composes orthogonally with visual token pruning.

cases.question: What does the paper say about predicting stock prices?
Which model is Apriel Voice built on?
cases.reference: The post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint.

cases.question: What is its average latency?
cases.reference: A mean latency of 1.91 seconds.

cases.question: What does it score on Big Bench Audio?
cases.reference: 98.90, in thinking mode.

cases.question: How many stages does the training have?
cases.reference: Two stages: one sets up the speech interface, the second adapts the projector and backbone together.

cases.question: How many authors wrote this paper?
cases.reference: 31 authors.

cases.question: What is SafeTulu?
cases.reference: A version of Tulu 3 with the 20% of examples most gradient-aligned with unsafe responses removed.

cases.question: How much does training on SafeTulu reduce attacks?
cases.reference: It reduces the GCG attack success rate by up to 22%.

cases.question: Which part of the model does SimpleLoRIF backpropagate through?
cases.reference: Only the final four transformer blocks.

cases.question: Which model families were tested?
cases.reference: Qwen, Llama and Olmo.

cases.question: What does O3PD train the student to reproduce?
cases.reference: The order of the teacher's top-K tokens, without fitting their probability values.

cases.question: Does O3PD need temperature tuning?
cases.reference: No. Its objective is invariant to the teacher temperature.

cases.question: What is the largest gain on AIME25?
cases.reference: Up to 5.6 points.

cases.question: How many teacher and student pairs were tested?
cases.reference: Six teacher-student pairs.

cases.question: What price per GPU hour did the authors pay?
Which number formats does FLAMIA support?
cases.reference: MXFP8, and a mixed NVFP4/FP8 training path.

cases.question: How much faster is it on B200?
cases.reference: 1.10 to 1.40 times faster for the combined forward and backward attention call.

cases.question: Which GPUs is it built for?
cases.reference: NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (B200 and B300).

cases.question: Which models were used to check training stability?
cases.reference: Llama-style models during pretraining.

cases.question: What does the paper say about training on AMD GPUs in 2019?
How much shorter are the answers on math?
cases.reference: Completion length drops by 41.7% to 45.4% on mathematics.

cases.question: Which training method is applied to the preference pairs?
cases.reference: DPO (direct preference optimization).

cases.question: Was LoCo trained on code?
cases.reference: No. It was trained only on math traces and still transfers to code generation.

cases.question: Where will the code be released?
cases.reference: On GitHub at github.com/MuyaoYuan/LoCo.
